## Objective
Turn the console hello world into a visually rich desktop app using only the JDK (Swing/Java2D, no dependencies). Running `Main` with no arguments opens a window; `Main --text` keeps the original console behaviour so it stays testable headless.

## Interface
- `src/Main.java`: `public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) }`. If `args` contains `--text`, print `Hello, World!` via `System.out.println` and return. Otherwise call `SwingUtilities.invokeLater` to create and show `FancyFrame`.
- `src/FancyFrame.java`: `public class FancyFrame extends javax.swing.JFrame { public FancyFrame() }`.
- `src/GradientPanel.java`: `public class GradientPanel extends javax.swing.JPanel` (package-private default package, like Main), with a public constructor `GradientPanel()` and a `public void start()` / `public void stop()` controlling its animation timer.
All files are in the default package (no `package` line), matching `src/Main.java`.

## Behavior
1. `GradientPanel` paints an animated background: a diagonal gradient whose hues slowly cycle over time, driven by a `javax.swing.Timer` (~30 ms), with antialiasing on.
2. It also draws a few softly translucent floating circles ("bokeh") that drift and wrap around the edges.
3. The centre shows the text `Hello, World!` in a large bold font with a drop shadow, and a pulsing (scale/alpha) effect.
4. `FancyFrame` hosts the panel, is undecorated-looking but still standard (title `Hello, World!`, 800x500, centred, `EXIT_ON_CLOSE`), and shows a smaller subtitle line plus a rounded "Click me" style button that changes the greeting among a small list of languages (Hello, Hola, Bonjour, Hallo, Ciao, こんにちは) each click.
5. The panel starts its timer when the frame becomes visible and stops it when the window closes.
6. `Main --text` prints exactly `Hello, World!` followed by a newline and never touches Swing, so it works on headless machines.

## Invariants
- No third-party libraries; compile with plain `javac src/*.java`.
- Painting code must not allocate heavy objects every frame beyond Graphics2D/gradient basics; all Swing work on the EDT.
- Keep code tidy and readable; short comments only where non-obvious.

## Edge cases
- Window resize: circles and text must adapt to the current panel size.
- Fonts missing the Japanese glyphs must not crash; fall back silently to the default font.

## Guardrails
- Do not write `.class` files into the repository.
- Do not add build files, tests or images.
- Do not modify anything outside the listed files.

## Out of scope
Automated GUI tests, packaging into a jar, sound, or settings persistence.
